5250.d:
Knifer, part I
Julije Knifer was a Croatian abstract painter and a founding member of the 1960s Croatian art collective Gorgona Group. The central motif of Knifer's art is the exploration of meander, a geometric form which he had been creating since 1960 in various painting techniques such as print, oil, acrylic paint, collage and mural. An example of which is the colossal meander created by Knifer on a 20 x 30 m canvas in a quarry in Tübingen (1975). His works can be found in Tate, MoMa and Centre Pompidou, amongst many museums.
Whole art life dedicated to rectangular meanders!

@uvdsc, 2021

5251.d:
A graphic poetry between order and chaos.

Voltaire, the philosopher, created the french word « Polytone » to define, in poetry, what is opposed to monotony. This generative work is an attempt to find it in a graphic poetry between order and chaos.

Format: 
Loop 400 frames - 50 FPS - 1000x1000px max. on screen.
By default the loop plays once then stops.

Controls with keyboard :
[p] -> play/pause animation (2 times when loop is off)
[l] -> on/off looping mode
[h] -> switch between 2 stop frames (when loop is off)
[s] -> Export HD capture (8000x8000px) when you want in the loop (only in « Open Live » mode)

Some features with probabilities:
2 colours background : Black (50%) or White (50%)
5 colours palettes : 2 monochrones (45%) or 2 duotones (30%) or 2 composed of 5 colours (25%)
6 pattern types for the image background (16.6% for all)
6 « noise » types : Crosses (26%) or Points (22%) or Line (18%) or Triangle (14%) or Circle (12%) or squad (8%) 
…

5256.d:
This work is an exploration of abstract landscapes using lines that are bounded to 8 directions. This limitation still allows for somewhat organic visuals and creates a visual language more akin to traditional drawing techniques.

Using a vector field with a noise function at different scales, I construct paths starting at random positions and moving to the neighbours cells pointed at by the vector field. Paths have a limitation of length and are bounded to the grid. I create tens of thousands of paths then render progressively on screen.

There are 10 parameters variations and 4 colors, 2 being rare and one very rare.

Original artwork by William Watkins · Lyon, 2021

5258.d:
The Andes range is a vast mountain range formed by a continuous system of mountains along the western coast of South America. The range is approximately eight thousand miles long. It is the longest mountain range in the world (in length).

Due to the extension towards the meridians, the Andes include different climatic zones. The climate (semi-arid) of the area varies constantly, as does its vegetation. Cold weather is prevalent, with high-altitude blizzards being very common.

This art tries to represent this important morphoclimatic formation of the earth!

5286.d:
A particle system implements an algorithm of attraction/repulsion forces, to give an harmonious movement to its sprites, interconnected between them like stems of a rhizome, shaping the blossoming of an abstract flower. 

Inspired by rhizomes and flowers, this generative art project runs in WebGL and uses Threejs as its library.

Variations include:
- Number of particles (in order of rarity, more particles means more rarity)
- intensity of connections between the particles
- colors
- the radius of the blossoming

A very rare amount of this generative token (<5%) are going to have a perfectly rounded shape. However, this is random, leaving it to the order/chaos balance.

This piece came to be as an adaptation of a workflow developed for an earlier Blender series, DeVoids.

The idea behind this technique is, instead of trying to create an image that fits to the needs, to modify and distort the UV Mapping of a 3d model.

UV Maps are usually though of as a needed step in creating a 3d asset, where you must achieve minimal distortion and minimize area losses. This piece explores narrative possibilities by ressignifying the tool usage.

Made in Cables.gl

The idea behind this technique is, instead of trying to create an image that fits to the needs, to modify and distort the UV Mapping of a 3d model.

UV Maps are usually though of as a needed step in creating a 3d asset, where you must achieve minimal distortion and minimize area losses. This piece explores narrative possibilities by ressignifying the tool usage.

Made in Cables.gl

* Change resolution: press 'd' followed by any number from 1 to 9 to add that amount to the pixel density. If you get a black screen you have surpassed what your graphics card can handle: press d + 0 to reset the pixel density. You can fine tune pressing d followed by + or - (+/- 0.5).
* Save image: press 's' to save the current image as png. For a higher resolution png, 1st increase the resolution using 'd' and then save the image with 's'.
* Tune image parameters: press 'z' (brightness), 'x' (contrast), 'g' (gamma), 'b' (blur) followed by + or - to adjust. Toggle tuning with 'a'. Press 'n' then + or - to adjust amount of noise.
* Redraw: 'r' (changes how lines are drawn)

It is recommended to read the full instructions on the article.

5345.d:
The <iframe> HTML element is an element that allows a web document to embed the contents of another web document within itself. iframes are at the core of fxhash. They are portals opening our view to rich content.

This work is a portal to itself. It loads itself within itself 20 times. It's not pretty, it reminds us of WordArt, it's a little bit hacky, it might break when our tools to display HTML will change. But it's a proof that the limits of our tools are only limits until creativity breaks them.

This work is not purely deterministic, because it simply cannot be. Slight timing differences due to loading times being different each time an <iframe> is loaded will make each visualization slightly unique.

If you view this token on mobile, the nesting limit was reduced to 4 to prevent performance issues.

This work is highly experimental. It leverages a "hack" to allow iframes to be nested.
Firefox max <iframe> nesting depth as of 28/12/2021 is capped at 9.
Works with chrome desktop 96.0.4664.110

5347.d:
Strange attractors throw shapes across the canvas and evolve over time.  Inspired by the 1997 'strange' screensaver from the xscreensavers collection.  

Four different attractor families, three scaling methods (to map the attractor to the finite canvas), seven colour schemes and infinite parameter combinations lead to unique and fascinating shapes and transitions.  The Clifford and de Jong attractors are represented, as well as two attractors of my own.  

The scaling methods are: 'linear' which simply scale the x and y axes by the maximum absolute values, 'arctan' which replaces x and y with atan(x) and atan(y) and 'sin' which replaces x and y with sin(x) and sin(y) to map them both to (-1,1).

Printed on the console you'll see which attractor you have, its equations, the range of values the parameters can take and the scaling method used.  

I hope you are inspired to learn about these systems.

All income from this token will be donated to foodbanks.

5370.d:
This piece features a GPGPU simulation the physarum polycephalum. A slime mold that can create efficient and beautiful networks.

In this piece, there are three colours of slime, each simulated individually on the GPU every frame. Each color has different attributes and behaviour and can infect the other colours, leading to colourful and organic looking movement and patterns. 

Since this simulation heavily relies on compute shaders to update all the individual slime in parallel, the preview did not get past the first few frames.

Requires WebGL2 and a fairly "modern" device to run (my 3 yr old 200$ phone runs it okayish). Please check if it works on your device before minting.

Rambles is an art project exploring the joy and variety of simply wondering from point to point.
Each Ramble is a 5x5 grid with properties determined and set at mint. Properties include the density of circle placement, palette selection, grid visibility and numerous other features, some rather unexpected and each defined by the spirit of randomness.
Rambles contract allows for a total of 20 possible palettes.
18 of these palettes have been carefully crafted for pleasing results. The last 2 palettes are relatively rare but truly strive to capture uncertainty and optimally fortuitousness. With that said, we make no guarantees on styling, only promising surprise and hopefully delight.

5444.d: "The Web of Chaos" by S. Liu stems from the cardioid curves, generated by a point on a circle rolling around a fixed circle of the same radius. By changing the rolling speed, we can discover novel symmetries resembling petals on flowers. To inject chaos into a given cardioid curve, we first shuffle x and y coordinates of each point on the curve and connect them using straight lines. We then rotate and translate the lines collectively to transform the interconnected bundle into a intriguing pattern. Finally, we animate the emergence of symmetric pattern by controlling speed and direction of the line rotations in order to give the audience the sense of time passing and the vivid elegance of dynamics on mathematical constructions.

aprendizajes is a generative art project that pays a tribute to the process of learning. 25% of primary proceeds go to Save The Children. Full description of the artwork+instructions here: https://www.iillucid.com/aprendizajes/

The artwork allows the user to:

* Change resolution: press 'd' followed by any number from 1 to 9 to add that amount to the pixel density. If you get a black screen you have surpassed what your graphics card can handle: press d + 0 to reset the pixel density. You can fine tune pressing d followed by + or - (+/- 0.5).
* Save image: press 's' to save the current image as png. For a higher resolution png, 1st increase the resolution using 'd' and then save the image with 's'.
* Tune image parameters: press 'z' (brightness), 'x' (contrast), 'g' (gamma), 'b' (blur) followed by + or - to adjust. Toggle tuning with 'a'. Press 'n' then + or - to adjust amount of noise.
* Redraw: 'r' (changes how lines are drawn)

It is recommended to read the full instructions on the article.

5461.d:
There is something almost subversive about generative art that mimics nature. Rather than excelling at abstract mathematical beauty, it tries to hold the complexity and elegance of the natural world, all while attempting to be interesting art. This makes it a different kind of challenge than the mathematical attractors and flow fields that are common across generative art.

It may be ironic then that the solution to natural forms is very often mathematical. The trees in this work are built recursively as a graph, much like how one could build a fractal. But chaos is mixed in at each step to allow the shapes to vary, and reduce their self-similarity. This is a different approach to L-systems but the results are very similar.

Connect: www.art.cmu.edu/people/golan-levin/
